method_summary: Frozen Xiaomi-Robotics-1-RoboCasa365 backbone (5B params: Qwen3-VL-4B VLM + 36-layer DiT action head reading the VLM's own KV-cache) fine-tuned with rank-4 LoRA adapters on the VLM's language_model attention/MLP layers only, plus Phasor's own sparse end-to-end memory core (ImprovedHGRNGate + ModernHopfieldLayer + adaptive gate) applied to pooled VLM hidden states as an additive consolidation-loss regularizer. The DiT action head is never modified -- verified on every training run via exact weight-sum matching before/after (87388.32329446077, unchanged in all runs).
training_data: Real RoboCasa365 pretrain_human300 corpus (all 300 tasks: 65 atomic + 235 composite, verified 300/300 present on disk and 0/16 composite_unseen tasks leak in, per robocasa.utils.dataset_registry.TASK_SET_REGISTRY['pretrain300']). This is the protocol-compliant training data -- see 'protocol_correction' below for the earlier, invalid 34-task version.
protocol_correction: The RoboCasa365 leaderboard maintainer (sepnasiriany) flagged on PR #16 that the original submission's fine-tuning data (34 atomic_seen+composite_seen tasks only) does not satisfy the official protocol, which requires training on the full pretrain_human300 corpus (300 tasks) -- restricting training to eval-overlapping tasks makes the numbers incomparable to other entries. Both ablation legs were retrained from scratch on the full pretrain_human300 corpus (same seed/budget: 220 steps, batch 48) and fully re-evaluated. The results below (*_pretrain300 entries) are the real, protocol-compliant, submittable numbers. The original *_realdata_fixed entries are kept below for historical record only and are marked invalid -- superseded.

baseline_frozen_xr1.description: Frozen Xiaomi-Robotics-1-RoboCasa365, no fine-tuning -- reference point.

lora_only_pretrain300.description: LoRA-only ablation, fine-tuned on the full, protocol-compliant pretrain_human300 corpus (300 tasks). This is the real, valid comparison point for isolating M7's specific contribution.
lora_only_pretrain300.note: The only one of the three legs (baseline / LoRA-only / LoRA+M7) to beat the frozen baseline overall, and has the strongest composite_unseen result of all three -- real, protocol-compliant evidence that plain LoRA fine-tuning on the full corpus modestly improves generalization to held-out tasks.

lora_plus_m7_pretrain300.description: LoRA + M7 memory-core consolidation, fine-tuned on the full, protocol-compliant pretrain_human300 corpus (300 tasks). This is the primary submission leg (Phasor_m7).
lora_plus_m7_pretrain300.note: HONEST FINAL VERDICT: M7's memory core does not add value over LoRA alone. LoRA+M7 beats baseline on composite_unseen (+0.75pt, so the memory core is not harmful) but underperforms LoRA-only on atomic_seen, composite_unseen (the generalization-relevant category), and overall -- only composite_seen favors LoRA+M7, by 0.5pt. LoRA+M7's overall result (56.76%) is slightly below the frozen baseline (56.88%).

lora_plus_m7_realdata_fixed_INVALID.description: Original LoRA+M7 leg, trained on only the 34 atomic_seen+composite_seen tasks. Flagged by the RoboCasa maintainer as not satisfying the official protocol (training data must be the full pretrain_human300 corpus, not a subset overlapping the eval tasks). Kept for historical record only -- do not cite as the submission result.

lora_only_realdata_fixed_INVALID.description: Original LoRA-only leg, same 34-task protocol violation as above. Kept for historical record only.
lora_only_realdata_fixed_INVALID.note: Eval sweep was stopped partway (1585/2500, ~63%) when the project pivoted to the pretrain300 retrain; never completed.

lora_only_realdata_INVALID.description: An earlier LoRA-only run affected by a since-fixed action-dimension field-order bug, abandoned early (487/2500 episodes, 1.4% success). Not usable as a comparison point.

training_config.lora_target_modules: VLM language_model attention (q_proj/k_proj/v_proj/o_proj) and MLP (gate_proj/up_proj/down_proj) Linear layers only
training_config.dit_action_head: frozen, untouched (verified via exact weight-sum invariant on every run)
training_config.training_data_pretrain300: Full RoboCasa365 pretrain_human300 corpus (300 tasks), same budget/seed as all other legs for direct comparability

notes: A real bug was found and fixed early in this project: code/robocasa_lerobot_dataset.py copied the raw lerobot 'action' parquet column directly into the model's action-head input, but the on-disk field order did not match the order the model's action head was actually calibrated against. Fixed by adding action_window_to_real_order(); verified via a 15/15 (100%) targeted smoke test before launching each full sweep since.

A second, more significant issue was found later: the original ablation's training data was restricted to the 34 atomic_seen+composite_seen tasks, which the RoboCasa maintainer correctly flagged as not satisfying the official protocol (training must use the full pretrain_human300 corpus). Both legs were retrained on the full 300-task corpus and re-evaluated; see the *_pretrain300 entries above for the real, submittable results.

Honest final verdict, on protocol-compliant data: LoRA-only fine-tuning on pretrain_human300 modestly beats the frozen baseline overall (+0.12pt) and on composite_unseen (+1.37pt). Adding M7's memory-core consolidation term on top does not improve on this -- LoRA+M7 underperforms LoRA-only on atomic_seen, composite_unseen, and overall, landing slightly below baseline overall. M7 is not harmful (it still beats baseline on composite_unseen) but does not add value beyond LoRA alone in this properly-validated setup.
